chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), is she from the four (permanent wives)? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, nor from the seventy.'

key_terms.السَّبْعِينَ: The seventy (referring to the distinct category or number associated with Mut'ah wives)
key_terms.الْأَرْبَع: The four (referring to the four permanent wives allowed in Islam)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of Mut'ah wives compared to permanent wives in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of women in *Mut'ah* (temporary marriage) by distinguishing them from the four permanent wives (*al-arba'*) mentioned in the Quran. By stating they are 'not from the seventy,' he indicates that *Mut'ah* women constitute a distinct legal category, separate from both the primary permanent wives and the broader group of seventy wives permitted to prophets, thereby affirming their specific jurisprudential ruling in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the Mut’a, is she from the four (allowable wives)?’ So heasws said: ‘No, nor from the seventy (i.e. as many as you so desire to)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from abu Basir who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
if al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) is of four. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, even seventy is not unlawful.’”
